text:
Aisha (eng-arch): Quick check — proposing we split the policy compiler from the runtime surface. TL;DR: move expressive policy logic to compile-time so runtime only runs a small decision graph.
Tom (eng-runtime): +1 to keeping runtime tiny. what does the runtime surface look like? deterministic, stateless?
Aisha (eng-arch): Minimal surface: inputs: request metadata (region, tier, token_budget, measured_latency); outputs: ordered candidate list + fallback hints. No long-running state.
Devin (eng-platform): Curious about rollout complexity. If compiler emits decisions, how do we patch rolling rules without a full deploy?
Linh (eng-runtime): We could support versioned decision blobs and hot-swap them from control plane. runtime validates signature then swaps. ops-bot: deploy-checklist: hot-swap supported, signature validated, metrics emitted.
Aisha (eng-arch): Exactly — compile -> sign -> release. runtime only trusts signed blobs and emits explainability traces.
Tom (eng-runtime): Tradeoffs: less dynamic (can't easily inject runtime telemetry-based tweaks), but simpler and lower p99 cost.
Devin (eng-platform): For dynamic adjustments (e.g., short-term regional congestion), we can layer a tiny override table in runtime: key->score delta, TTL. Keep it limited.
Linh (eng-runtime): Agree. Override table should be small, memory-bounded, and controlled by ops. No Turing-complete logic.
Aisha (eng-arch): Also want deterministic fallbacks for cost/latency: compiler emits primary candidate + ordered fallback list with constraints. runtime selects first compatible.
Tom (eng-runtime): Example compiled blob snippet:```policy_blob
version: 2
candidates:
  - id: redwood-v2
    constraints: { region: eu-west, max_latency_ms: 150 }
    priority: 10
  - id: redwood-v1-quant
    constraints: { quantized: true }
    priority: 5
fallbacks:
  - id: cheaper-small
    reason: cost_over_budget
```
Devin (eng-platform): We should include guardrails: compiled blob must include a semantic hash of policy source + author + automated tests run id. traceability matters.
Aisha (eng-arch): Observability hooks: runtime emits both "chosen_candidate" and "rejected_candidates" with rejection reason tags (latency_violation, cost_cap, region_mismatch). That helps compiler rework.
Linh (eng-runtime): What about per-tenant custom policies? We can't compile for every tenant on demand at runtime. Suggest per-tenant overrides stored as small deltas (adopt same signature model).
Tom (eng-runtime): Performance target: additional 0.4ms median decision time vs current routing. How much complexity in parsing blob? use protobuf or compact binary.
Devin (eng-platform): Protobuf + gRPC watch for blob updates. Signed blobs stored in control-plane S3 with version metadata.
Aisha (eng-arch): Security: KMS-signed blobs and runtime verifies on load. Also include a revocation window for emergency disable.
Linh (eng-runtime): Edge case: incompatible version -> runtime returns soft-fallback to a safe default route and emits alert. ops-bot: AUTO-ALERT created if runtime rejects >0.1% of blobs.
Devin (eng-platform): Testing: compiler should run a "simulated traffic" harness to ensure fallback coverage and no cycles in fallback graph.
Tom (eng-runtime): Implementation steps: 1) define minimal runtime API 2) protobuf schema + signature 3) control-plane compile+sign pipeline 4) watch + hot-swap + override table 5) rollout canary.
Aisha (eng-arch): Risks: 1) ossing too much flexibility at runtime 2) mismatch between simulated traffic and production 3) operational burden of compiling and signing. Mitigations linked to each risk.
Devin (eng-platform): Can we ship a small PoC in staging that only handles cost-tiering (cheap vs standard) to validate end-to-end?
Linh (eng-runtime): Happy to own runtime bits for PoC. I'll sketch proto and perf budget.
Aisha (eng-arch): Sweet. Action items: Aisha -> draft RFC for compiler-to-runtime blob format; Linh -> proto + perf bench; Devin -> control-plane sign/watch plan; Tom -> define fallback semantics and safe default.
Tom (eng-runtime): I'll add a short checklist in the RFC for canary rollout.
Devin (eng-platform): cc @ops-bot for automated checks.
ops-bot: noted — will create canary monitor and deployment guardrails when RFC is posted. :robot_face:
Aisha (eng-arch): Thanks all. Will post RFC draft by EOD tomorrow. :thumbsup:
